Use case: stylized-concept, character sheet using exact supplied style/layout.
Asset type: one original game-operator character sheet, landscape 1536x1024 PNG.
INPUT IMAGE 1 is the ADOPTED PROTAGONIST STYLE AND LAYOUT REFERENCE. Match its rendering, stylized adult proportions, slightly enlarged expressive head/hands, crisp designed cloth fold planes, sculpted hair shapes, broad clean matte shading, restrained material textures, soft neutral studio lighting and plain blue-grey backdrop EXACTLY. This is a member of the very same cast rendered by the same artist. Stylized neither anime nor photographic. No painterly brush/grunge overlay, no realistic skin pores or micro-wrinkles, no cel-outline illustration; match the reference's polished designed 3D/game-character aesthetic.
INPUT IMAGE 2 is OLD IDENTITY / PACK REFERENCE ONLY. Keep that person's age, ethnicity, recognizable hair and eyewear, body type, and owner-specific pack concept, but replace its photographic rendering and drab clothing treatment with image 1's adopted style and the current outfit/colors below.
LOCK THE SHEET LAYOUT to image 1: large full-body FRONT at left and BACK in center at the same height, complete crown-to-boot framing; a single unmasked head-and-shoulders portrait at UPPER RIGHT; and a smaller full-body elevated three-quarter REAR view at LOWER RIGHT, camera about 50 degrees downward above horizontal, showing crown, shoulders and pack top with foreshortened legs/boots. Keep the same relative view sizes, panel positions, sheet margins, background and soft contact shading. Main views in a confident relaxed neutral stance, hands loosely slightly off hips and a gentle weight shift, not a T-pose or action scene. Exactly these four depictions of ONE consistent person/design. No text, borders or panel labels.
Match the protagonist's equipment design language: compact local-computer hiking-backpack scale, practical protected heat vents, tidy cables, straps and connectors, but make this owner's pack individually recognizable. The pack is worn in all three full-body views. No screen, face, eyes, glow or hologram.
Cool first: strong readable simple clothes, a restrained single accent color against dark neutrals. No team uniform, no orange accent copied from the protagonist, no white-and-red corporate palette. No extra props, weapons, tools, cap, full-backstory costume, logos, emblems, brand marks or watermark.
CHARACTER: the WRITER, a Black woman in her early 30s, deep warm brown skin, short natural tightly curled dark hair, lean build. Preserve image 2's recognizable woman and glasses, restyled to the adopted protagonist's proportions and level of polish. A quietly confident, intelligent and approachable expression; an adult, not a teenager. Hair visible with the hood resting down behind her neck.
SIGNATURE: large bronze/gunmetal ROUND prescription glasses with an additional pair of ROUND flip-up INFRARED lenses on little upper hinges, raised above the clear viewing lenses so her eyes stay visible. This is two paired circles of optical hardware, not decorative horns or goggles. Keep the same glasses/raised IR attachments across views and portrait.
MASK: a MAGENTA bandana pulled up over her nose and mouth in the FRONT, BACK and battle-camera body views. In the upper-right portrait the SAME bandana is DOWN around her neck, revealing her whole face; glasses remain on.
OUTFIT: a fitted waist-length charcoal/slate hooded jacket, clean designed silhouette, sleeves pushed just below elbows; a dark warm-grey plain tee, fitted dark charcoal trousers and practical dark umber boots. Subtle small black INK SMUDGES on a few fingertips and at one cuff only, the sole nod to printing. No apron, notebooks, newspaper costume or overall grime.
ACCENT: rich printer-ink MAGENTA on the bandana, one small jacket zipper pull and a short restrained inner-hood piping accent. Most fabric and stitching remain dark neutral and tonal; no full magenta coat or magenta seam network.
BACKPACK: smaller, slimmer and lighter than the protagonist's, muted moss/olive-grey with two subdued stitched repair patches, protected heat vents and a few neatly secured dark cables. One small folded paper tucked under a side strap; no extra dangling papers or props. It must look practical, loved and repaired, but stay cleanly readable in the adopted stylized rendering.
Output ONE writer sheet matching image 1's style/layout, with the writer identical in all four views.
